Values used are the wavenumbers re-tabulated by Murphy & Berengut (arXiv:1311.2949) and the 1414(8) MHz quoted by Filippin et al. (arXiv:1604.07594); these two differ by ~4 MHz for 26-24.
Beverini et al. 1990 (285 nm 24Mg absolute frequency / isotope shifts): no openable page with the numbers found (Springer and ADS abstract pages blocked).

25Mg 3s3p 1P1 hyperfine constants (Kluge & Sauter, Z. Phys. 270, 295 (1974), level crossing): Springer abstract page blocked, Crossref/Semantic Scholar carry no abstract. A web-search snippet gave A = -7.7(5) MHz and 16 MHz > B > 0, but the page could not be opened, so it is NOT recorded as data.

3s3p 1P1 lifetime by Liljeby et al. 1980 (beam-foil) and Kelly & Mathur 1980 (Hanle): no opened page states the lifetimes; only Lurio 1964 recorded (matrix elements from other experiments are in arXiv:physics/0102070 Table IV, see level note).

Hyperfine constants of 25Mg 3s3d 3D1,2,3: no measurement found. Therkildsen and Jensen theses (2009) report the 3P-3D 383 nm 25Mg spectra as unexplained (fine and hyperfine splitting comparable) and give no A/B. He et al. PRA 80, 024501 turned out to cover only the 3P-4s 3S1 (517 nm) lines, not 383 nm.
25Mg-24Mg isotope shifts on the 383 nm 3P-3D lines: only 26-24 (Hallstadius 1979) found; a search snippet for 'Measurement of the (3s3p)3P1-(3s3d)3D1 isotope shift in Mg I' could not be opened.
Direct measurement of the 458 nm clock-line isotope shift: none found; 26-24 and 25-24 entries are computed combinations from Friebe et al. 2011 Table 2.

Measured Lande g_J factors (e.g. 3P1, 3P2 from Lurio 1962; 1P1 from level crossing): the NIST levels file has no g column, but no opened source states measured g_J values (Lurio 1962 full text is paywalled; abstract has none).
Natural lifetime of 3P0 in bosonic 24Mg/26Mg: no value (strictly forbidden single-photon decay); only the 25Mg hyperfine-quenching theory is recorded.

Madsen et al., J. Phys. B 33, 4981 (2000) (photo-ionization of 3s3p 1P1 at 285 nm): abstract not retrievable (IOP/Crossref/Semantic Scholar); the absolute cross section in notes is from the follow-up Madsen & Thomsen, J. Phys. B 35, 2173 (2002) abstract.
Sterr et al. 1993 and Godone & Novero 1993 originals not opened; their numbers are taken as quoted by Friebe et al. 2008/2011 and Kulosa et al. 2015 (method 'compilation').
Single-channel A coefficients for 517 nm / 383 nm lines: not duplicated (NIST ASD lines file carries Aki); Aldenius branching fractions + lifetimes are given instead.
notes: Isotope shifts are nu(first) - nu(second) in MHz. On 1S0-3P1, 1S0-3P0, 1S0-1P1 and 3P-3D the heavier isotope lies at HIGHER frequency (positive 26-24); on the 517 nm 3P-4s 3S1 triplet the heavier isotope lies at LOWER frequency (negative 26-24): He et al. print unsigned 'Delta 24-26' values and the sign was fixed from Hallstadius & Hansen as quoted by Berengut et al. 2005 / Aldenius et al. 2007. Frequencies refer to 24Mg unless an 'isotope' key says otherwise; NIST level energies in this file are natural-mixture values copied from data/nist/Mg_I_levels.tsv. frequency_THz values given with wavenumber_cm were converted with c = 299792458 m/s. Entries with method 'compilation' were read in a later paper/thesis that quotes the original experiment (original named in 'source'). Fields marked 'derived here' are simple differences/centroids/1-over-rate of quoted numbers. Non-schema keys used: alternatives, note, natural_linewidth_MHz, magic_wavelength_nm, quadratic_zeeman_MHz_per_T2, lattice_light_shift_slope, hyperfine_components_25Mg_MHz, wavenumber_cm, intercombination_decay_rate_s, unc_plus/unc_minus, nuclear_moment_muN. 3P1 lifetime: experiments (4.0-5.3 ms) sit above most theory (2.8-3.8 ms). 4s 3S1 lifetime: experiments scatter 9.7-14.8 ns. 3P2 lifetime 2050 s is for 24Mg; 25Mg is shortened by hyperfine quenching (theory). Photoionization: Mg is ionized by resonance-enhanced two-photon ionization at 285 nm: 3s2 1S0 -> 3s3p 1P1 (35051.264 cm^-1) followed by a second 285 nm photon into the continuum (2 x 35051 cm^-1 > limit); isotope-selective by tuning the first step (isotope shifts 0.73 and 1.41 GHz, ~80 MHz natural width) - Kjaergaard, Hornekaer, Thommesen, Videsen, Drewsen, Appl. Phys. B 71, 207 (2000), https://phys.au.dk/fileadmin/site_files/forskning/iontrap/pdfs/Isotope_Kjaergaard_ApplPhysB_71_2000.pdf (in an ion trap the 280 nm Mg+ cooling light can also provide the second photon). Absolute photo-ionization cross section of 3s3p 1P1 at 285 nm: (8.1 +- 2.3)e-17 cm^2, Madsen & Thomsen, J. Phys. B 35, 2173 (2002), abstract at https://www.osti.gov/etdeweb/biblio/20277584 ; this two-photon ionization is the dominant loss of 285 nm Mg MOTs (Therkildsen thesis). First ionization limit Mg II (3s 2S1/2): 61671.05(3) cm^-1, 'Limit' row of data/nist/Mg_I_levels.tsv (NIST ASD, https://physics.nist.gov/PhysRefData/ASD/levels_form.html ; Kjaergaard et al. show E0 = 7.65 eV).
